THE FIRST FULLY HEADLESS CASE: the driver was written by SEAM_A through agent/seams.py (Path A) with no human or in-conversation authoring, and the deterministic stages were driven by agent/run_worklist.py. discovery.discovery_method: GitHub code search for setCodePointLimit, dated and screened, then traversal-confirmed against the 1.32 boundary.

library._baseline_note: 1.30 is the version this client was actually on before it crossed the boundary, read from its own recorded crossing rather than from the catalog's generic runnable_baseline.
library.breaking_boundary: 1.32 (3 MiB / 3145728 code-point ceiling imposed by default)
library.dependency_scope: compile, declared directly via the <snakeyaml.version> property in pom.xml

in_repo_version_transition._note: The parent commit already declares 1.32, so the client had been living with the ceiling for a year before the fix. State 2 runs exactly that configuration: their pre-adaptation code on the version they were actually shipping.

behavioral_break.mechanism: snakeyaml 1.32+ caps incoming documents at 3 MiB (3145728 code points) BY DEFAULT. GlobalConnectionServer read plugin descriptors as `new Yaml(new SafeConstructor()).load(...)` — no LoaderOptions — so the ceiling applied the moment the version crossed 1.32, and any plugin.yml above 3 MiB stopped loading.
behavioral_break.observed_exception: de.cubeside.globalserver.plugin.PluginDescriptionException: Could not load the plugin.yml in the plugin jar ...: The incoming YAML document exceeds the limit: 3145728 code points. — caused by org.yaml.snakeyaml.error.YAMLException with the same message
behavioral_break.blast_radius: Any plugin whose plugin.yml exceeds 3 MiB. PluginDescription is the single entry point for every plugin the server loads, so a single oversized descriptor breaks plugin loading rather than one feature.

adaptation.repo_note: A Minecraft-ecosystem connection server with a plugin system; single-module Maven.
adaptation.shape: RAISE_THE_LIMIT — the default production path is restored for every caller with no configuration required, in both PluginDescription and GlobalServer.
adaptation._commit_message_note: The message is a bare 'Update dependencies' and the commit also bumps log4j and jline. The snakeyaml change is not incidental to it though: the same commit adds LoaderOptions to BOTH yaml call sites and raises two separate limits, which is a deliberate response to the resource caps rather than a mechanical version bump.

verification.method: 3-state differential, one driver source compiled and run unchanged in all three states
verification.driver_summary: Builds a real jar containing a plugin.yml of just over 4 MiB (valid name/main/version fields plus one long scalar) and calls the production constructor `new PluginDescription(jar)`. A jar rather than a string fixture because the production path reads from a JarFile entry and nothing else.
verification.driver_provenance: Written by SEAM_A headlessly. It found this entry point from the adaptation diff alone — and independently arrived at the same design as the hand-authored Path B driver in this directory (GlobalConnectionServer_BbcTest.java), which was written earlier without either seeing the other.

verification.oracle: 1 PASS / 2 FAIL with the catalogued signal / 3 PASS — satisfied
verification.reproduced: Twice, on independent Path A runs. The first needed one SEAM_B fixture revision; the second passed on SEAM_A's first attempt once the framework hint was fixed.

_why_state_3_runs_at_2_2: State 3 runs at snakeyaml 2.2, not at the 1.32 boundary, because THE ADAPTATION DOES NOT WORK AT 1.32. It sets the limit on a LoaderOptions handed to `new Yaml(new SafeConstructor(options))`, and at 1.32 that Yaml constructor builds its own default LoaderOptions for the reader — so the constructor's options are ignored and a 4 MiB document still throws. The same code works from 2.x, which is what this commit actually bumped to. Running state 3 at the boundary would measure an adaptation this client never shipped; running it at 2.2 measures the one they did. Confirmed empirically: an earlier run with state 3 pinned to 1.32 failed with the identical signal.

harness_interventions.what: A test-scoped junit:junit:4.13.2 dependency was injected into the POM, identically at all three states.
harness_interventions.why: This client declares no test framework at all — log4j, jline, semver4j, mariadb and snakeyaml, and nothing else — so surefire would run nothing and a differential that runs nothing proves nothing. JUnit 4 rather than Jupiter because Maven's super-POM binds surefire 2.12.4, which cannot run Jupiter; pinning a newer surefire is a much larger change to the client's build than adding one test-scoped jar.
harness_interventions.affects_result: no — version-neutral with respect to snakeyaml, applied identically to every state

harness_interventions.what: bbc/BbcTest.java was written into src/test/java as an untracked file.
harness_interventions.why: SEAM_A: the driver has to exist somewhere, and untracked means it survives the checkouts between states.
The user-level settings mirror every repository through Central, which breaks any client declaring its own. Not load-bearing for this client, but applied uniformly across the corpus.
